subject: Centella Health — Monitoring, Alerting & Reporting RFI
messages:
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha.gupta@centellahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@centellahealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFI — Monitoring & Reporting Requirements

Hi Sean,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Procurement and our InfoSec team have compiled a short RFI to understand Redwood's operational monitoring and reporting for content safety and high-risk misuse scenarios. We're on a tight timeline for our vendor selection and would appreciate responses by the end of next week. High-level asks below — attached is our standard template (centella_rfi.xlsx).

1) Telemetry: what events are logged for inference requests (inputs, outputs, model id/version, inference latency, token counts, decision flags)? Retention periods and export formats?
2) Misuse detection: ability to flag policy violations in real time vs post-hoc; available signal types (toxicity, sexual content, illicit behavior, medical advice), and thresholds you surface to customers.
3) Alerting & SLA: alerting primitives (webhooks, email, PagerDuty), typical time-to-alert for high-priority incidents, and SLA coverage for hosted/dedicated deployments.
4) Evidence package: what artifacts can you provide for an audit (sample logs, transcripts, redaction support, user-submitted evidence handling)?
5) Reporting cadence & custom reports: can we schedule daily/weekly exports filtered by account/route?

Also, please indicate any operational constraints (PII redaction, data residency, on-prem options) and attach your monitoring matrix if available.

Thanks — cc'ing our security alias.

Best,
Aisha
Aisha Gupta
Sr. Procurement Manager, Centella Health
attachments: centella_rfi.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RFI — Monitoring & Reporting Requirements

Aisha — thanks for the detail and the template. We're happy to respond and have attached a concise monitoring matrix (redwood_monitoring_matrix.xlsx) that maps telemetry, retention, alerting, and export formats to the items in your sheet.

Quick summary upfront:
- Telemetry: our hosted and dedicated offerings log per-request metadata (model id/version, prompt and generated output hashes, per-token latency, token counts, KV-cache metrics, detection flags from the policy classifier). Raw texts are stored only when customers opt into transcript retention (configurable per-route). Default retention: 30 days for hosted trial accounts, 365 days for enterprise by contract; configurable to customer requirements (including on-prem).
- Misuse detection: real-time policy checks via a lightweight classifier run inline (latency optimized) plus a parallel asynchronous evaluator for more expensive detectors. Customers can subscribe to both streaming flags (webhook) and batch reports. We surface severity (info/warn/critical) and rule-ids for tracing.
- Alerting & SLA: built-in webhooks and email; PagerDuty integration available for Dedicated deployments. For critical policy incidents we recommend a push alert + evidence bundle; our typical time-to-alert for injected policy-critical signals is under 60s on Dedicated and under 90s on Hosted (subject to routing). SLAs differ by contract; Dedicated customers can opt into a 99.9% alert delivery SLA and 24/7 escalation support.
- Evidence: we can provide JSONL transcripts, redacted and unredacted logs (subject to contract), and per-request request/response hashes for integrity. For audits we produce an evidence package with hashes, timestamps, and the relevant model version.
- Reporting: scheduled exports (S3, secure FTP, or Drive link) can be configured daily/weekly with account + route filters. Custom reporting work is offered as a professional services engagement if you need tailored formats.

I'm looping in Jonas (Security) for specifics around telemetry formats, retention controls, and sample evidence artifacts, and Marissa (CS) to coordinate an evidence handoff and any customer-side retention/configuration settings. Would you be available for a 30-min call next Thursday to walk through the matrix?

Attachments: redwood_monitoring_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1-415-555-0198

Subject: RE: Initial RFI — Monitoring & Reporting Requirements

Hi Aisha / Sean — adding technical detail below to cover the telemetry/schema and evidence artifacts requested. I'm including a small telemetry sample as an attachment (telemetry-sample.jsonl).

1) Telemetry schema (high level):
- request_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), account_id, route_id, model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, response_hash, input_token_count, output_token_count, latency_ms, policy_flags: [{rule_id, severity, score}], inference_node_id, geo_region
- We publish both human-readable JSON logs and compressed JSONL bundles for bulk export. Logs can be emitted to customer-owned S3 buckets (preferred for Dedicated / Private) or streamed via secure webhook to your SIEM.

2) Retention & redaction:
- Retention windows are contractually configurable. We support policy-driven redaction at ingestion (PII detection using named-entity heuristics) and also provide reversible tokenization for customers who require the ability to rehydrate content during a legal review (subject to key management agreements). Default enterprise retention: 365 days, with options: 90 / 365 / indefinite (on-prem).

3) Misuse detection architecture:
- Inline classifier: a low-latency model that evaluates every request and emits discrete flags. Tunable thresholds per-account and per-route.
- Async scoring pipeline: runs heavier detectors (multi-model ensembles) for post-hoc analysis, generates batch reports and signals for human review workflows.

4) Alerts & delivery guarantees:
- Delivery: webhooks (HMAC-signed), email, PagerDuty. For webhooks we support retry/backoff and dead-letter S3 buckets for failed deliveries.
- Prioritization: critical policy violations are routed to a dedicated alerting tier (separate queuing and higher CPU/GPU allocation) to reduce time-to-alert.

5) Evidence artifacts for audits:
- Automatic evidence bundles include: request/response JSONL, policy classifier outputs, model version + container image id, server-side logs, and cryptographic hashes. For legal/e-discovery we provide chain-of-custody metadata and time-synced system snapshots.

6) Sampling & cost controls:
- Customers can set sampling rules (e.g., all high severity, 5% random samples, or n-of-m per-account) to balance cost and coverage.

7) Compliance posture:
- We maintain SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; penetration test reports available under NDA. For EU accounts we have region-restricted hosting and can offer on-premise deployment for PHI-sensitive workloads.

Notes: attached telemetry-sample.jsonl shows typical per-request log; redwood_monitoring_matrix.xlsx maps your RFI rows to these fields. If you need a worked example of an evidence package for a simulated misuse incident, we can prepare a red-team sample next week.

Attachments: telemetry-sample.jsonl (jsonl)

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Sean / Jonas — thank you, this is excellent and helps clarify a lot. A couple quick follow-ups before we schedule a call:

- For the reversible tokenization rehydration you mentioned, can you confirm whether KMS is customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) in the Dedicated offering? If so, what key rotation/retirement processes do you support?
- For webhook deliveries: can you provide an example HMAC header and retry behavior (number of retries/backoff) in writing so our infra team can validate?
- For the evidence package: would you be able to provide a red-team sample incident (anonymized) and a corresponding evidence bundle ahead of our vendor short-listing next week?

If you can answer those three items and drop a proposed time for a 30-min walkthrough, we'll move to scheduling. Procurement would like any contract-level retention options captured in writing (we'll use that in the SOW).

Thanks again — cc'ing our security and procurement aliases.

Best regards,
Aisha
Sr. Procurement Manager, Centella Health
